stories.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season continues Sunday with 14 games, including nine in the early window, and we'll have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In the early window, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn returns to face his former team in the Detroit Lions, and Tennessee Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll is facing off against the team that fired him during the season last year, the New York Giants.

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys will take their talents to Rio de Janeiro in one of four games in the second window before the Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams in primetime to cap off the day.

Be sure to check back after 1 p.m. ET when games start for updates.

stories.headline: What to watch during MLB's final day of the 2026 season
stories.summary: There's still much to play for entering the final day of the regular season. We have your guide to the last few games of baseball before October.
stories.body:
We're down to the final day of the regular season and still have two playoff spots to decide. The Cleveland Guardians clinched the AL Central on Saturday night while the Philadelphia Phillies are trying to avoid an epic collapse in the NL wild-card race.

Let's run down what's at stake on the final day, in the playoff races and on the individual side of things.

Playoff tracker | WS pressure rankings

Playoff races

NL wild card

San Diego Padres: 90-71 (vs. Arizona)

Chicago Cubs: 88-73 (vs. Boston in Tampa)

Philadelphia Phillies: 87-74 (vs. Tampa Bay)

Arizona Diamondbacks: 86-75 (at San Diego)

Tiebreakers: Cubs over Phillies; Diamondbacks over Phillies

The Padres clinched the No. 4 seed with their win on Saturday night over the Diamondbacks, snapping Arizona's six-game winning streak. That means the Padres get to host the wild-card series against the Cubs, a clear advantage since San Diego is 50-30 at home and 40-41 on the road. Clinching before Sunday was big as well, since they can now rest all their top relievers for a couple days before the playoffs begin Tuesday.

The Cubs can't be too happy. The game against the Red Sox had been rescheduled for Tampa due to the storm pelting the Northeast, but since the Cubs own the tiebreaker over the Phillies, it's now a completely meaningless game for both teams.

Boos rained down on the Phillies from their home fans in a sorry 12-1 loss to the Rays on Saturday. They've scored three runs in losing four games in a row, have gone 9-14 in September, and have hit just .220/.299/.341 in the month, the worst OPS in the majors. But they still control their own destiny. Unfortunately, not clinching means they now have to start Zack Wheeler on Sunday, which will make him unavailable for the wild-card series, unless he starts Game 3 on short rest. Cristopher Sanchez started Friday, so he presumably won't be ready until Game 2, leaving Aaron Nola - who started and pitched one inning on Saturday, allowing three runs - as the likely Game 1 starter if the Phillies get there.

The Diamondbacks need to beat the Padres and have the Phillies lose and they're in. The Diamondbacks and Phillies split their season series, but the Diamondbacks own the tiebreaker by virtue of a better intradivision record (they're 32-19 against the NL West while the Phillies finished 28-24 against the NL East). The Diamondbacks played a sloppy game on Saturday, with outfielders losing two balls in the lights, and will send Michael Soroka to the mound on Sunday against Randy Vasquez for the Padres. Arizona ace Eduardo Rodriguez started Thursday, so he's lined up for Game 1 of the wild-card series if the Diamondbacks advance.

AL West race

Houston Astros: 80-81 (at Athletics)

Texas Rangers: 80-81 (at Twins)

Tiebreaker: Astros over Rangers

Well, we're guaranteed a non-winning division winner for the first time in MLB history. The worst record for a division winner belongs to the 2005 Padres, who took the NL West with an 82-80 record. The Astros win the division with a victory on Sunday or a Rangers loss. Houston did win 13-2 on Saturday -- but haven't won two games in a row since Sept. 2-4.

The Astros start Peter Lambert against Seth Johnson, in a bullpen game for both teams. Lambert started on Thursday against the A's and threw 62 pitches, allowing four runs in 2.2 innings, so he'll be pitching on two days' rest, hoping to go a couple innings before the Astros turn the game over to their bullpen. No doubt, Joe Espada will try to get more than one inning from his top relievers, Bryan Abreu and especially Josh Hader.

The Rangers will start MacKenzie Gore, who allowed two runs in five innings in his last start but has had abbreviated outings of late, pitching just 11 innings across his three previous starts. Expect a run of relievers for the Rangers. Their top guys all pitched in Saturday's win over the Twins but weren't needed in Friday's blowout loss, so there are no major usage issues to worry about there.

AL Central race

Cleveland Guardians: 85-76

Chicago White Sox: 83-78

The Guardians clinched on Saturday with a win over Kansas City combined with the White Sox losing to the Rockies.

Winning the division was huge for Cleveland. First, the Guardians get the No. 2 seed and a bye into the division series and the opportunity to rest their pitching staff. It also saves Stephen Vogt the decision of having to use rookie ace Parker Messick on Sunday to clinch the division. Conceivably, Messick might have started and the Guardians still could have lost the division which would have left Messick then unavailable for the wild-card series. Now he'll be more than ready for Game 1 of the ALDS.

The White Sox, meanwhile, will give all their top pitchers some much needed rest to get ready for the AL West winner on Tuesday.

National League seeding

Milwaukee Brewers: 102-59

Los Angeles Dodgers: 99-62

Atlanta Braves: 94-67

The Brewers clinched the top seed last Thursday and will play the winner of the Padres-Cubs series while the Dodgers will play the winner of the Braves and Phillies/Diamondbacks.

How has the top overall seed done in the postseason? While baseball's playoffs are widely regarded as more of a random tournament than other sports, over the past 10 seasons, four of the top teams did win the World Series and two others reached it. Of course, there have always been the anomalies like 2021 when the Braves won it all after finishing the regular season with the 12th-best record in the majors, or 2023, when we had a wild-card matchup between the Rangers (tied for sixth-best record) and Diamondbacks (tied for 12th).

Jacob Misiorowski will start Sunday for the Brewers. He last pitched a week ago, when he threw 44 pitches in three innings while pitching on four days' rest for the first time since July 7. The first game of the NLDS won't be until next Saturday, so that would give Misiorowski five days of rest before his Game 1 start. Like his last outing, it might be an abbreviated outing to keep him as fresh as possible for that game.

Of note: The NL division series schedules have one less off day than the AL series, with off days after Games 2 and 4, so Misiorowski would likely return in a potential Game 5, pitching on five days' rest. In the AL, the Game 1 starter could return for Game 4 on four days' rest. For the Brewers, that also means they will need four starters in the NLDS, when only Misiorowski and Logan Henderson look dependable right now. Dustin May hasn't gone more than three innings in any of his past three starts, which could push Robert Gasser into the No. 3 hole. Kyle Harrison did pitch two scoreless innings on Saturday, but he had been so bad in recent outings that he's likely just a candidate for the bullpen.

What else is at stake

Yordan Alvarez tries to lock up the MVP

A few weeks ago, this was a Triple Crown chase, but now the Astros slugger will likely have to settle for the MVP Award instead. The question: Do the Astros need to win the division for him to win? I don't think so. While we're likely to see a scattered vote, with Alvarez, Junior Caminero, Bobby Witt Jr. and maybe Cam Schlittler all receiving first-place votes, Alvarez is probably the only player who is going to land first or second on just about every ballot. Alvarez (.316) does hold a 10-point lead over Chandler Simpson (.306) for the batting title and is one home run behind Pete Alonso, so could still take two of the three Triple Crown categories.

Other statistical races

AL home run race: Alonso has 43 while Alvarez and Caminero have 42. Ben Rice has 41.
NL home run race: Pete Crow-Armstrong and Kyle Schwarber are tied with 45. Schwarber is looking to lead for the second straight season and third time since he joined the Phillies in 2022. He's one of those Phillies mired in a deep slump though: He hasn't homered in 10 games.
NL batting race: Gabriel Moreno (.311) has overtaken Luis Arraez (.310), who hasn't played since spraining his ankle on Thursday. Arraez is going for his fourth batting crown while Moreno would be the first catcher to lead since Buster Posey in 2012.
Alonso chasing history: With an eight-RBI lead over Alvarez, he'll become the first player to lead both leagues in RBIs after leading the NL with 131 in 2022 while with the Mets.
NL RBI race: Alec Burleson (116) leads Sal Stewart (111) after driving in runs in four consecutive games. Stewart was trying to become the first rookie to lead his league since Walt Dropo of the 1950 Red Sox (some guy named Ted Williams is the only other rookie to do it).
MLB strikeout leader: Cleveland's Gavin Williams leads Misiorowski, 248 to 247, so Miz should pass him even with an abbreviated appearance on Sunday. Misiorowski also leads Schlittler for the overall MLB lead in ERA, 1.86 to 1.94.
A swing and a miss: Colston Montgomery has already broken Mark Reynolds' strikeout record, whiffing 225 times to Reynolds' 223.

Saying goodbye to Justin Verlander ... and now Max Scherzer

Justin Verlander had an emotional goodbye on Saturday in Detroit and now Sunday may be the final appearance for Scherzer, who will start for the Blue Jays. Scherzer has yet to announce his retirement, saying this week that he's going to make his decision in the offseason.

"I've gone through ups and downs throughout the season, I get it, but I've gotten to the point where I'm pretty healthy," he said on Saturday. "I've talked to everybody in my inner circle and we all kind of feel the same way. We don't need to make a decision today. Get to the offseason and see how things unfold."

Verlander looked like a potential 300-game winner back in 2019, when he had 225 wins through his age-36 season and was coming off a 21-win and Cy Young season for the Astros. But he pitched just once in the COVID-shortened 2020 season before his elbow surrendered to time and then missed all of 2021. Remarkably, he came back and won another Cy Young Award in 2022 with an 18-win season and career-low 1.75 ERA. Three hundred wins remained a possibility -- and a goal.

But he would go just 22-27 over the next four seasons so finishes with 266 wins, tied with Bob Feller and Eppa Rixey. After Scherzer and his 224, next on the active wins list are Gerrit Cole at 163 and Chris Sale at 159. We're only not going to see a 300-game winner for ... well, who knows when ... we may not see a 200-game winner for a long time. Indeed, Verlander and Scherzer will go down as perhaps the last of the true workhorses, guys who pitched 200-plus innings - and more at their peak - year after year.

stories.headline: Islanders sign Logan Stanley to one-year contract
stories.summary: The Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.
stories.body:
The New York Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.

The No. 18 overall pick in 2016 by the Winnipeg Jets, Stanley, 28, was dealt to the Buffalo Sabres last season at the trade deadline. He finished the season with seven goals and 26 points, both career highs, while finishing a two-year, $2.5 million contract.

But Stanley struggled in the postseason and was scratched in Buffalo's final four games of a Round 2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He skated in eight playoff contests, accumulated 19 penalty minutes and finished with a minus-2 rating.

The Islanders, who have missed the playoffs the past two seasons and brought in Peter DeBoer as their new head coach, open the regular season Wednesday at the Toronto Maple Leafs.

A left-shot defenseman who is a native of Kitchener, Ontario, Stanley has international experience playing for Team Canada. In 2016, he played in the world junior championships, when Canada finished fourth.

stories.headline: Lando Norris subjected to online abuse after calling for Franco Colapinto ban, Alpine 'condemn' hate
stories.summary: Lando Norris has been subjected to a torrent of online abuse after he called on Formula 1 to serve Argentine driver Franco Colapinto with a ban.
stories.body:
Lando Norris has been subjected to a torrent of online abuse after he called on Formula 1 to serve Argentine driver Franco Colapinto with a ban.

World champion Norris made the claim after Colapinto triggered a three-car pileup which forced him to retire from Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

However, Norris' comments provoked a bombardment of online hate toward the British driver across his social media channels -- largely from supporters of Colapinto.

The Alpine driver accepted fault for the collision and will serve a five-place grid penalty at the next round.

Responding to the wave of abuse circulating online, Colapinto's Alpine team issued a statement to the Press Association on Sunday.

In it the team said: "As a team, we feel it's necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula 1 community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula 1, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Alpine to consider next steps after Colapinto, Gasly DNF

- Kimi Antonelli dawns on 'worst' race weekend of the season despite gaining 11 places

"We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula 1 is renowned for and what makes it so special."

Norris' failure to finish in Baku leaves him 116 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings and his title defence all but over.

George Russell claimed his third win of the season to trim Antonelli's advantage from 81 points to 66 with a possible 208 still remaining over the eight scheduled rounds.

Russell is now Antonelli's sole realistic title contender and the Briton will bid to use Saturday's win as a springboard to continue his championship comeback -- starting at next weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Key questions, takeaways from Sunday's Game 1s
stories.summary: From the first tipoff to the final buzzer, we've got everything you need to know for Sunday's openers.
stories.body:
After a thrilling end to the regular season in which the playoff seeds were not all determined until late into the night of the final days of games, the highly anticipated 2026 WNBA playoffs are here!

First up are the best-of-three first-round series -- No. 1 Minnesota Lynx vs. No. 8 New York Liberty, No. 2 Golden State Valkyries vs. No. 7 Dallas Wings, No. 3 Las Vegas Aces vs. No. 6 Indiana Fever and No. 4 Atlanta Dream vs. No. 5 Washington Mystics -- all of which begin Sunday.

Game 2 will take place Tuesday for Minnesota-New York and Las Vegas-Indiana and Wednesday for the other two series. Game 3s, if necessary, would be held Thursday and Friday.

ESPN experts Kendra Andrews, Kareem Copeland, Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel dissect what to expect from the biggest stars and top teams in the first round of the playoffs and for the rest of the postseason.

MORE: Playoff predictions | Strengths, flaws for every team | Top 25 players | Schedule

Top-seeded Minnesota hasn't looked dominant in recent weeks. What are the biggest concerns the Lynx have?

Philippou: Coach Cheryl Reeve has had some memorable news conferences this year, including Aug. 6 after Minnesota's loss to the Sparks when she said, "We lost our game because we don't play any f---ing defense. So, if you want to talk about offense, you sound like the players." Reeve has not been pleased with the team's defensive performance since early July, with its rating on that side of the floor ranking seventh in the league in that span (it was No. 1 in the WNBA in May and June). Reeve was even upset about the team's defensive effort in its penultimate regular-season game against the Connecticut Sun; the Lynx bounced back in a big way by holding the Fever to 66 points on Thursday. Undoubtedly, Reeve will be keeping a close eye on the defense starting in this first-round series against the Liberty -- hardly a typical No. 8 seed -- but also for the rest of the postseason should the Lynx advance.

Voepel: Consistency was Minnesota's hallmark for much of the season, but that changed in late August. The Lynx lost four of their last six regular-season games, with two of those losses coming before the FIBA World Cup break and two after. Minnesota averaged 90.8 points this season, but only 76.3 in those four losses. If the Lynx fall short of a title, it might be due to their offense not producing at the level it did for much of the regular season. As Alexa said, Reeve has placed the blame on defense, saying the problems there have slowed down the offense. But in Minnesota's last six regular-season games, Napheesa Collier averaged just 13.0 points. Collier, who was out until July 22 after ankle surgery, needs to return to her superstar scoring form.

Copeland: The Lynx would like to see Collier take another step forward in her return from surgery. Collier said last week that she feels as good as she has all season, and she's trying to get as close to 100% as possible. The five-time All-Star is moving better and quicker and is a veteran in Cheryl Reeve's system, but Collier acknowledged that getting used to the tendencies of Olivia Miles and Natasha Howard has been a learning experience. The Indiana Fever held Collier to single-digit scoring performances in the last two regular-season games, and the Lynx need her to be a bit closer to her typical dominant self.

Andrews: Miles' status is a bit concerning. She missed the last two regular-season games because of a left calf injury, and though the Lynx say it's not serious and she will play in the postseason, those soft tissue injuries are tricky. Players usually have to wait until it's fully healed, and playing on it before it's 100% could cause more damage. Perhaps Minnesota was playing it safe by holding out Miles so she would be healthy for Game 1. But, either way, the Lynx need her on the floor -- and they need her at her best -- for a deep run.

Which team has the most momentum and which has the least entering the playoffs?

Copeland: The Mystics are a league-best 16-4 since July 20. Their current four-game win streak is the second longest in the WNBA. (The Aces are on a seven-game win streak, but that run doesn't include a victory vs. a playoff team.) Washington mixed in a season-defining 93-77 win against the Fever less than a week ago. The Mystics are the youngest team in league history to reach the postseason and are having unexpected success for Year 2 of a rebuild. Washington has leaned on its defense, which has the No. 2 rating in the league (103.3) while allowing the second-fewest points (82.7).

Philippou: Since the WNBA season resumed after the World Cup break, the Atlanta Dream have led the league in net rating (31.2, albeit in just four games). Their 4-0 record in that span includes two road wins over the Liberty, one of which was without Breanna Stewart. Las Vegas and Washington are the only other undefeated teams in September, and the Lynx, Liberty and Fever are each 2-2. That Minnesota is 2-4 in its final six regular-season games is of note: Only one team in league history -- the 2021 Chicago Sky -- won the Finals after finishing with a losing record in their final six games of the regular season.

If the top-seeded Lynx don't win the title, which team will?

Philippou: History tells us that the champion will likely be the No. 1 or No. 2 seed, which this year means the Lynx or Valkyries. In this current playoff format, only one team outside the top 2 seeds has won the WNBA title: the 2021 Sky, who were a No. 6 seed and faced the fifth-seeded Mercury in the Finals. That was also the only time in this format that any teams outside the top-four seeds even reached the Finals. Still, with how tight the standings have been this year -- the top-four seeds are all separated by three games, the top six by five, and Nos. 5-8 by two -- maybe precedent goes out the window.

Copeland: The road to a title still goes through Las Vegas, and any championship hopeful will have to pry the trophy from A'ja Wilson. The league's active dynasty has won three of the past four titles and been to four Finals since 2020. Wilson, the four-time MVP and two-time Finals MVP, was a rookie the last time the Aces didn't at least reach the semifinals. The loss of starting forward NaLyssa Smith (noncontact left leg injury) was a significant blow, but the trio of Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray -- a combined 10 championships, 17 All-Star appearances and six gold medals -- has found success with different supporting casts. History is also on the line as the Aces can tie the Houston Comets, Seattle Storm and Minnesota Lynx with a league-record four titles.

Which player might have the biggest impact on the postseason?

Philippou: I have my eye on Miles, who will be appearing in her first WNBA postseason, while dealing with a calf injury that kept her out of the Lynx's last two regular-season games. She has been even better than expected as a rookie and has had some clutch regular-season performances. But how will that translate in the postseason and in a series setting where opponents have more opportunities to adjust to her? Perhaps it won't have any bearing, but in her one Elite Eight game during her college career, Miles and TCU suffered a blowout loss to South Carolina.

Copeland: Is it Jackie Young's turn for a Finals MVP? Wilson has two, and Gray got hers in 2022. Young averaged career highs in points (18.9), assists (6.8) and 3-pointers made (2.3) this season, and was fourth in the league in assists and 10th in points. Young is one of the best two-way guards in the world, and the Aces need her to play like it. Remember, she had 32 points and 10 assists in the Game 5 overtime closeout against the Fever in the 2025 semifinals, then averaged 20.3 points, six assists and five rebounds in the Finals sweep over the Mercury.

Voepel: It might seem boring to pick A'ja Wilson, but the best player in women's basketball has consistently been great in the postseason. Wilson remains hungry for championships and has an enormous impact offensively and defensively.

Andrews: I am really excited to see Angel Reese in her first postseason. She racked up double-doubles during the year, but it seems as though she has played at a different level the last week of the season. Unlike Wilson or Young, Reese doesn't have a plethora of postseason experience, but the way she has elevated the Dream this season is undeniable. They look primed to make a big playoff push, and she has been one of their most critical players.

Which first-round series are you most excited for, and what storyline are you most looking forward to seeing throughout the playoffs?

Philippou: The star power in the Aces-Fever series is historic: Per Elias, two of the three highest-scoring duos in league history will be competing against each other in the first round: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell have combined for 47.0 points per game this year, and Jackie Young and A'ja Wilson are averaging a combined 45.1 points. It's wild to think that either Mitchell-Clark-Aliyah Boston or Wilson-Young-Chelsea Gray will not advance to the semifinals, but that's the nature of the playoffs for you.

Voepel: The Aces-Fever series is atop the marquee for the reasons Alexa stated. It also will be interesting to see how two of the youngest teams in the playoffs -- Washington and Atlanta -- compete against each other. The Dream have not advanced to the semifinals since 2018, when the Mystics beat them. Washington last made the semis in 2019, when it went on to win the WNBA title. Atlanta's Angel Reese and Washington's Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen, all members of the winning U.S. World Cup team, will make their playoff debuts.

Copeland: New York's inconsistencies have people questioning the Liberty, but this is still a first-round rematch of the 2024 Finals, which went to overtime in Game 5. The majority of the key figures are still here -- Breanna Stewart, Jonquel Jones, Sabrina Ionescu, Napheesa Collier, Kayla McBride, Courtney Williams. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve acknowledged a respectful yet "healthy dislike" for each other. That sounds like a lot of fun for a high-stakes, three-game series. But the Aces' quest for a fourth championship and A'ja Wilson's continued persistence to surpass every other all-time great remain the storyline for me.

Andrews: I agree with Kareem's first pick: Lynx versus Liberty. Yes, it's a 2024 Finals rematch. Yes, it's a collection of the best players in the league. But I feel these teams have the most to lose. If the Lynx fail to get out of the first round, they will face a plethora of offseason questions, including why they couldn't get the job done again despite being the No. 1 seed. If the Liberty lose, it will be their second straight year not advancing out of the first round. A year ago, that cost Sandy Brondello her job, and it will surely raise more questions for New York this year.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

Brownlow Medal: Nick Daicos. He's the best player in the game and it's not particularly close. Could easily win four or five of these throughout his career.

Coleman Medal: I wonder if Sam Darcy could have won it this year if he hadn't suffered a season-ending ACL injury ... I'll pick him again for 2027.

stories.headline: Host Jalen Brunson gets assist from Knicks on 'SNL' premiere
stories.summary: Jalen Brunson had four of his Knicks teammates -- Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart -- in the audience for his monologue Saturday night, in his role as host of "SNL."
stories.body:
Jalen Brunson brought four of his NBA champion teammates to "Saturday Night Live."

The reigning NBA Finals MVP had four of his New York Knicks teammates -- Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart -- in the audience for his monologue Saturday night, in his role as host of the NBC program's 52nd season premiere.

Brunson poked fun at how he's not going to sing, how ESPN's Stephen A. Smith -- a Knicks fan, portrayed during the monologue by longtime "SNL" star Kenan Thompson -- owed him an apology for questioning his abilities and even quipped about how much he's looking forward to getting back to the Knicks' home court at Madison Square Garden.

"The exact spot where Taylor and Travis got married," Brunson said, referring to the summer wedding of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce at the team's arena.

But the best assists came from Towns, Bridges, Anunoby and Hart, who all asked Brunson questions as part of the monologue.

Towns asked if someone could foul out of "SNL." When told it's not possible, Towns said, "So I can be here, like, the whole show? Nice."

Bridges asked Brunson if his arms were long, but lamented that he'll never fly. Anunoby, who got a huge ovation, asked Brunson if he recalled missing a shot late in Game 4 of the NBA Finals against San Antonio -- a series that the Knicks won in five games. The Game 4 shot that Anunoby was referring to was a last-second tip-in -- off a Brunson miss -- that basically ensured the Knicks would win the game.

"That was awesome," Anunoby said.

Hart, who co-hosts a podcast with Brunson, asked his New York teammate about how he left $113 million on the bargaining table when signing with the Knicks. Brunson, in turn, asked why Hart poked Brunson in the backside when the Knicks won the NBA Cup last season.

Brunson then brought his teammates to the stage for one last roar from the crowd.

Brunson became the first active NBA player to host the show since LeBron James -- then of the Cleveland Cavaliers -- in 2007, and the first pro athlete in the role since Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs' tight end, in 2023.

The other NBA players to host besides Brunson and James: Michael Jordan in 1991, Charles Barkley on four occasions (including one as an active player in 1993) and Bill Russell in 1979. Russell's stint came 10 years after he retired as a player.

Brunson, Jordan, Barkley and James all hosted season premieres of "SNL." And Brunson promised to step up late, just like what he delivered in crunch time of the Knicks' games in the title series against the Spurs in June.

"I'm going to approach this the same way I approach a Knicks Finals game," Brunson said. "The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful. The last sketch is going to be amazing."

stories.headline: What We Learned: Twelve-man Knights defy belief; Smith books Roosters reunion
stories.summary: The Newcastle Knights have completed one of the most remarkable turnarounds in NRL history, stunning minor premiers Penrith. Three things we learned.
stories.body:
Accor Stadium, SYDNEY -- From wooden spooners to Grand Finalists.

The Newcastle Knights have completed one of the most remarkable turnarounds in NRL history, stunning minor premiers Penrith 20-14 despite playing the final 44 minutes with 12 men.

Phoenix Crossland was sent off for the hip-drop tackle which left Nathan Cleary with a serious leg injury, but the Knights overturned an eight-point half-time deficit to reach their first Grand Final since 2001.

They will now face the Sydney Roosters, setting up an extraordinary reunion for former Tricolours halfback Sandon Smith.

Here are three things we learned from Sunday's preliminary final.

NEWCASTLE'S FAIRYTALE IS NOW SO MUCH MORE

This is no longer a fairytale.

Newcastle's place in the Grand Final was earned through courage, resilience and sheer defiance.

The Knights had every reason to fall apart after Crossland's dismissal in the 36th minute. Their hooker was gone, Penrith had an extra man and Blaize Talagi's ensuing penalty goal handed the Panthers the lead.

When Lindsay Smith crashed over shortly before halftime, Penrith led 14-6 and appeared ready to clinically dismantle another challenger.

Instead, the Knights produced a second half that will live permanently in the club's history.

Dominic Young finished one of the tries of the season just three minutes after the restart, handling twice in a sweeping movement that began inside Newcastle's half and also involved Sandon Smith, Dane Gagai and Francis Manuleleua.

It was a statement of intent. The Knights were not going to spend the remainder of the contest desperately protecting their line and waiting for Penrith to finish them.

Even when they were forced into survival mode, their scramble was extraordinary.

Kalyn Ponga and Manuleleua held Casey McLean up by millimetres. Greg Marzhew rushed in to pressure a pass intended for an unmarked Brian To'o. Dylan Lucas followed an error with a shot that forced Lindsay Smith to spill the ball, while Ponga folded Moses Leota with one of the defining tackles of the afternoon.

Newcastle defended their two-point advantage for more than 20 minutes despite playing a man down, then sealed the result through Smith at the death.

This was not a fortunate side falling into a Grand Final.

The Knights eliminated South Sydney, survived a sold-out Eden Park and then conquered the minor premiers with 12 men.

Justin Holbrook inherited the wooden spooners less than 12 months ago. He now has Newcastle 80 minutes from a premiership.

SANDON SMITH HAS EARNED THE ULTIMATE REUNION

Of all the possible Grand Final storylines, Sandon Smith facing his former club might be the most compelling.

Smith left the Roosters at the end of last season in search of the opportunity to control his own side. On Sunday, he proved he is capable of controlling the biggest games.

With Newcastle trailing 14-10 after an hour, Penrith conceded a penalty for high contact on Fletcher Sharpe.

As Billy Phillips and Moses Leota turned their backs and waited for the kick to touch, Smith saw something nobody else did.

He tapped the ball, accelerated through a vacant defensive line and raced 50 metres untouched to score beneath the posts.

Penrith were furious. Newcastle were level. Smith calmly converted his own try to put the Knights ahead.

It was a moment of audacity from a halfback who refused to allow the occasion, or his side's numerical disadvantage, to make him conservative.

Smith then produced the decisive play in the dying moments, securing possession and racing away for the try which finally ended Penrith's resistance.

His impact extended beyond the scoreboard.

With Crossland dismissed and Fletcher Sharpe enduring some untidy moments, Smith became Newcastle's organiser, primary kicker and calming presence. He repeatedly drove Penrith into their own corners and trusted his depleted defensive line to keep turning the Panthers away.

The 23-year-old will now enter a grand final against the club where his NRL career began.

The Roosters know better than anyone what Smith can do.

They will now have to stop him from completing one of rugby league's great revenge stories.

PENRITH'S LOSS FEELS SECONDARY TO CLEARY'S INJURY

Nathan Cleary entered the contest under an injury cloud and began the match on the bench as Penrith attempted to manage a stress-related issue in his foot.

He entered after 26 minutes.

Ten minutes later, Penrith's season, and potentially the immediate future of their champion halfback, was turned upside down.

Cleary became trapped in a tackle involving Crossland and Manuleleua, with Crossland's weight falling across the playmaker's lower leg.

The reaction was immediate. Cleary remained on the turf in severe distress as medical staff rushed onto the field, before he was taken from Accor Stadium on a medicab and transported to hospital.

Early reports indicated a suspected compound fracture, while Crossland was sent off for the hip-drop tackle.

The confronting incident left players from both teams visibly shaken and stripped the preliminary final of much of its celebratory atmosphere.

Penrith's injury toll worsened in the 67th minute when Talagi went down without contact and was assisted from the field with a suspected Achilles injury.

The Panthers still had enough opportunities to win.

McLean was held up centimetres short. Jack Cogger dropped the ball at second receiver with Penrith attacking. Luke Garner's pass to an unmarked To'o was called forward, and several other promising sets ended with basic errors.

Those moments will frustrate Ivan Cleary. Penrith played more than half the match with an extra man and failed to score a single point after the break.

For so long, their defining quality has been an ability to remain composed while opponents unravel around them. On Sunday, confronted by injuries, a desperate defensive line and a Knights side with nothing to lose, Penrith became the frantic team.

Their second consecutive preliminary-final defeat confirms that the seemingly automatic march to grand final day is over.

For now, however, the end of Penrith's season is not the greatest concern.

The health of their champion halfback is.

stories.headline: MLB, White House discuss playing game at national park
stories.summary: The White House said in a statement that MLB asked the administration about hosting a game at a national park, adding that the National Park Service has not granted a permit to do so.
stories.body:
Major League Baseball has approached the Trump administration about hosting a game at a national park, officials from the White House and the league confirmed to The Washington Post on Saturday.

The White House said in a statement that MLB asked the administration about hosting a game at a national park, adding that the National Park Service has not granted a permit to do so.

"This is not a Presidential directive, nor is it being directed by the White House. It's also not being driven by the Department of Interior," the statement said. "Therefore, this is not a White House or Administration priority."

However, two sources told the Post that the Trump administration has scouted locations in Grand Teton National Park, located in northwest Wyoming, to build a baseball park. Sources told the Post that National Park Service deputy director Frank Lands visited Grand Teton National Park this week and looked at three potential locations to hold a baseball game within the park's boundaries. Lands declined comment to the Post.

The discussions come as MLB has expanded its use of single-game sites over the past decade. MLB returned for the Field of Dreams game and Little League Classic this year, played inside the Bristol Motor Speedway in 2025 and held a game at Rickwood Field in Birmingham, Alabama, in 2024.

An MLB official, speaking anonymously, told the Post that playing at a national park was one of several ideas under consideration by the league. The 2027 schedule has been released, with games at the Field of Dreams and Little League Classic both set for August, so the possibility of a new game site may be unlikely until at least 2028.

Donald Trump has made major changes to the National Parks Service during his second term, including major cuts to the budget and staffing. The administration has also looked at selling or giving Parks land to private development.

But for now, an MLB game on federal land is just in the idea stage.

"If the MLB wants to go on site visits of national parks, that is their prerogative," the White House said in its statement.

stories.summary: Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.

stories.headline: JJ Gabriel and the 'nightmare' battle for Premier League academy talent
stories.summary: In the fiercely competitive race for the best Premier League academy players, JJ Gabriel won't be the last young talent at the center of a transfer tug-of-war.
stories.body:
The battle for talent is intense in the Premier League.

Manchester City and Manchester United went head-to-head for Elliot Anderson in the summer. Chelsea and Arsenal fought it out for Morgan Rogers.

But the race to sign the world's best players is only part of it. There's also a scramble for players tipped to become stars of the future.

Manchester United are still dealing with the fallout of 15-year-old JJ Gabriel's decision to leave Old Trafford. The forward is yet to make a competitive first-team appearance, but losing a young player considered to be one of the best in Europe for his age is still a significant blow.

The fear for United is that a highly rated prospect who has been in their academy system since the age of 11 goes on to fulfill his potential elsewhere. Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and a host of Premier League clubs have already registered interest in securing Gabriel's signature.

United are proud of their record of having at least one academy graduate in every matchday squad since October 1937. The inclusion of Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Shea Lacey at Fulham on Sunday took the run of matches to 4,368.

Producing players is important for every club and can save millions in transfer fees. But it means there's pressure to identify, sign and retain the right ones, which is much harder than you'd think even for clubs of Man United's caliber.

How does youth development work?

Under the Elite Player Performance Plan, introduced in 2012, youth development in England is split into three phases: foundation phase (U9 to U11), youth development phase (U12 to U16) and professional development phase (U17 to U23).

Academies are separated into four categories. The biggest clubs -- such as Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool -- oversee Category 1 academies, which can cost more than £2 million per year to run.

Premier League heavyweights can coach players from any age, although they're not allowed to play official matches until U7s. Before reaching U9s, players can train anywhere and often attend sessions at different academies to find the best fit. They can be formally registered with a club for the first time at the U9 level.

Players can sign a full-time scholarship -- which includes training and education -- as U16s, at which point they're officially allowed to be paid. Before then, financial inducements can include things such as travel expenses, and this element can sometimes lead to a bending of the rules. There are stories of some clubs paying for chauffeured limousines to get players to training or offering executive tickets for matches.

A professional contract can be offered to a U16 player, but can't be signed until a player's 17th birthday. Young players can't employ an agent until they're 16 and can't make a senior appearance in the Premier League until the season they turn 16.

When does the battle for players start?

There's a race among teams to get the best talents through the door of an academy around age 7. It gives clubs the chance to have a closer look at players and impress parents before formal registration at U9.

It is then that clubs and players make their first big decision, and for some, it's the only one they make. For example, Manchester City ended their recent Carabao Cup tie against Norwich with four players on the pitch who had been part of their setup since they were 8 -- Nico O'Reilly, Rico Lewis, Floyd Samba and Kaden Braithwaite.

For clubs, retaining players year after year is just as important as recruiting. Gabriel was close to leaving United in summer 2025. City believed there was a chance of prying him away to the other side of Manchester, only for Jason Wilcox, United's director of football, to get involved and persuade Gabriel to stay.

Even at that point, United knew they would face another fight to keep him in summer 2027. With Gabriel eligible to sign scholarship forms after his 16th birthday -- on Oct. 6 -- there was always a chance he could be tempted by other offers.

With compensation due for any player who moves clubs from U9, United will get a payment from Gabriel's next club if he leaves. But it will be nothing compared to the transfer fee he could command if he turns into the player many expect him to become.

Rio Ngumoha joined Chelsea's academy at age 8 before moving to Liverpool at age 15 in 2024. Liverpool were ordered to pay minimum compensation of £2.8 million in February 2026. Now 18 and already capped by England, his transfer value (according to Transfermarkt) is more than £25 million.

The impact of Brexit

Things changed for Premier League academies when the United Kingdom left the European Union on Dec. 31, 2020. Until then, clubs could sign European-based players at 16, and it was something United took advantage of to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Atletico Madrid. Cesc Fabregas moved to Arsenal from Barcelona in 2003 in the same way.

One source told ESPN that being able to recruit from the rest of Europe was "a safety valve" when the right domestic players weren't available. But with that avenue closed starting in January 2021, more emphasis has been placed on finding players locally. Catchment areas are usually considered to be anything within an hour's travel time to a club's training base, per the rules, because clubs practice up to three times per week.

These rules mean that there are particularly fierce battle grounds in places where a number of big clubs operate within the same broad geographical area. According to one source, northwest England -- where United, City, Liverpool and Everton compete for the same players -- is "a nightmare." London has more clubs, but with a bigger population, there are more players to go around.

Do youngsters have player power?

Some do and some don't. According to research by the University of Essex in 2024, around 97% of youngsters who go through Category 1 academies never make a Premier League appearance. Around 50% leave or are released before they turn 16.

But with just a small number destined to make the grade, clubs have to spend a lot to sign the best. Multiple sources have told ESPN there have been instances of players demanding first professional contracts worth £50,000 a week, as well as backdated bonuses. One source described salaries at youth level as having gone "through the roof."

Players and parents often also want to know that there's a pathway to the first team. According to sources, part of the reason Gabriel has become unsettled at United is because of a perceived lack of opportunities -- despite being just 15.

He made his senior debut in a preseason friendly against Atletico Madrid, but that was the only action he saw over the summer. United also chose not to register him for the UEFA Champions League, meaning he was ineligible to play against Sabah FK on Sept. 10. After the game against the Azerbaijan champions, Gabriel removed any mention of United from his social media and the club was made aware of his desire to leave.

United insist they have done everything possible to keep him happy. Gabriel and his family feel certain promises have been broken.

Now exploring his next move, Gabriel has every major club in Europe battling for his signature. He won't be the last youngster at the center of a transfer tug-of-war before his senior career has even begun.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.
